original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-duality-compact-support}
Let $p : U \to \Spec(k)$ be separated of finite type where $k$ is a field.
Let $\omega_{U/k}^\bullet = p^!\mathcal{O}_{\Spec(k)}$.
There are canonical isomorphisms
$$
\Hom_k(H^i(U, K), k) =
H^{-i}_c(U, R\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_U}(K, \omega_{U/k}^\bullet))
$$
of topological $k$-vector spaces
functorial for $K$ in $D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_U)$.
statement:
For a separated finite-type scheme $U/k$, a bounded coherent complex $K$, and an open compactification $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ with $X$ proper over $k$, choose any Deligne system $(K_n)$ extending $K$. Define *compactly supported coherent cohomology* $H^i_c(U,K)=\varprojlim_n H^i(X,K_n)$, a topological $k$-vector space with the projective-limit topology of finite-dimensional discrete $k$-vector spaces. This is independent of compactification and Deligne representative up to its canonical pro-identifications. For an arbitrary $k$-vector space $V$, give its full linear dual $V^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_k(V,k)$ the limit topology over the finite-dimensional subspaces of $V$, discrete on each finite-dimensional dual. For a separated finite-type morphism $p:U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, write $\omega^\bullet_{U/k}=p^!k$, where $p^!$ is the upper-shriek functor built using a proper compactification. For every $K\in D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_U)$ and $i\in\mathbf Z$ there is a *canonical functorial isomorphism of topological $k$-vector spaces*
\[
\operatorname{Hom}_k(H^i(U,K),k)\xrightarrow{\sim}
H_c^{-i}\!\left(U,R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(K,\omega^\bullet_{U/k})\right).
\]
The left dual has the weak inverse-limit topology above, not the unrestricted discrete topology when $H^i(U,K)$ is infinite-dimensional. The cohomology on the right is computed using coherent pro-extension, not classical étale cohomology with compact supports.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-duality-compact-support-restrict-open}
With notation as in Lemma \ref{lemma-duality-compact-support}
suppose $U' \subset U$ is an open subscheme. Then the diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
\Hom_k(H^i(U, K), k) \ar[rr] & &
H^{-i}_c(U, R\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_U}(K, \omega_{U/k}^\bullet)) \\
\Hom_k(H^i(U', K|_{U'}), k) \ar[rr] \ar[u] & &
H^{-i}_c(U', R\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_{U'}}(K, \omega_{U'/k}^\bullet)) \ar[u]
}
$$
is commutative. Here the horizontal arrows are the isomorphisms of
Lemma \ref{lemma-duality-compact-support}, the vertical arrow on the
left is the contragredient to the restriction map
$H^i(U, K) \to H^i(U', K|_{U'})$, and the right vertical arrow
is Remark \ref{remark-covariance-open-lower-shriek} (see discussion
before the lemma).
statement:
For a separated finite-type scheme $U/k$, a bounded coherent complex $K$, and an open compactification $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ with $X$ proper over $k$, choose any Deligne system $(K_n)$ extending $K$. Define *compactly supported coherent cohomology* $H^i_c(U,K)=\varprojlim_n H^i(X,K_n)$, a topological $k$-vector space with the projective-limit topology of finite-dimensional discrete $k$-vector spaces. This is independent of compactification and Deligne representative up to its canonical pro-identifications. For an arbitrary $k$-vector space $V$, give its full linear dual $V^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_k(V,k)$ the limit topology over the finite-dimensional subspaces of $V$, discrete on each finite-dimensional dual. For a separated finite-type morphism $p:U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, write $\omega^\bullet_{U/k}=p^!k$, where $p^!$ is the upper-shriek functor built using a proper compactification. Let $U'\hookrightarrow U$ be an open subscheme of a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, $K\in D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_U)$, and $K'=K|_{U'}$. Write $D_U=R\mathcal Hom_U(K,\omega^\bullet_{U/k})$, so $D_U|_{U'}\simeq R\mathcal Hom_{U'}(K',\omega^\bullet_{U'/k})$. Then the square
\[
\begin{matrix}
\operatorname{Hom}_k(H^i(U,K),k)&\xrightarrow{\sim}&H^{-i}_c(U,D_U)\\
\uparrow&&\uparrow\\
\operatorname{Hom}_k(H^i(U',K'),k)&\xrightarrow{\sim}&H^{-i}_c(U',D_U|_{U'})
\end{matrix}
\]
commutes, where the left upward arrow is the *linear dual of restriction* $H^i(U,K)\to H^i(U',K')$ and the right upward arrow is the *covariant open-immersion* map for compactly supported pro-cohomology. Both horizontal maps are the natural topological duality isomorphisms.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-h0-compactly-supported}
Let $X$ be a proper scheme over a field $k$. Let
$K \in D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_X)$ with $H^i(K) = 0$
for $i < 0$. Set $\mathcal{F} = H^0(K)$.
Let $Z \subset X$ be closed with complement $U = X \setminus U$.
Then
$$
H^0_c(U, K|_U) \subset H^0(X, \mathcal{F})
$$
is given by those global sections of $\mathcal{F}$ which
vanish in an open neighbourhood of $Z$.
statement: For a separated finite-type scheme $U/k$, a bounded coherent complex $K$, and an open compactification $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ with $X$ proper over $k$, choose any Deligne system $(K_n)$ extending $K$. Define *compactly supported coherent cohomology* $H^i_c(U,K)=\varprojlim_n H^i(X,K_n)$, a topological $k$-vector space with the projective-limit topology of finite-dimensional discrete $k$-vector spaces. This is independent of compactification and Deligne representative up to its canonical pro-identifications. For an arbitrary $k$-vector space $V$, give its full linear dual $V^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_k(V,k)$ the limit topology over the finite-dimensional subspaces of $V$, discrete on each finite-dimensional dual. Let $X$ be proper over $k$, $Z\subseteq X$ a closed subset, and **$U=X\setminus Z$** (correcting the self-referential typo '$U=X\setminus U$' in the pinned source). Let $K\in D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X)$ have $H^i(K)=0$ for all $i<0$, and set $\mathcal F=H^0(K)$. The natural covariant map $H_c^0(U,K|_U)\to H^0(X,K)=H^0(X,\mathcal F)$ is injective, and its image consists precisely of global sections of $\mathcal F$ whose restrictions vanish on some open neighbourhood of $Z$. Equivalently its image is the intersection of the images $H^0(X,\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)\to H^0(X,\mathcal F)$ over all $n$, where $V(\mathcal I)=Z$.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-lichtenbaum}
Let $U$ be a variety. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_U$-module.
If $H^d(U, \mathcal{F})$ is nonzero, then $\dim(U) \geq d$ and if
equality holds, then $U$ is proper.
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $U$ a *variety over $k$*, meaning an integral separated scheme of finite type over $k$ in the Stacks convention. Let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_U$-module and $d\ge0$. If $H^d(U,\mathcal F)\ne0$, then $\dim U\ge d$ (Grothendieck vanishing). If equality $\dim U=d$ holds, then $U$ must be **proper over $k$**. Equivalently, on a nonproper variety of dimension $d$, the top coherent cohomology $H^d(U,\mathcal F)$ vanishes for every coherent $\mathcal F$.

If equality $\dim U=d$ holds, then $U$ must be **proper over $k$**. Equivalently, on a nonproper variety of dimension $d$, the top coherent cohomology $H^d(U,\mathcal F)$ vanishes for every coherent $\mathcal F$.

conclusions: Dimension at least d and properness when dimension exactly d.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{theorem-lichtenbaum}
Let $X$ be a nonempty separated scheme of finite type over a field $k$.
Let $d = \dim(X)$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $H^d(X, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ for all coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules
$\mathcal{F}$ on $X$,
\item $H^d(X, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ for all quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules
$\mathcal{F}$ on $X$, and
\item no irreducible component $X' \subset X$ of dimension $d$
is proper over $k$.
\end{enumerate}
statement: Let $X$ be a **nonempty separated finite-type** scheme over a field $k$ with Krull dimension $d=\dim X$. The following conditions are equivalent: (1) $H^d(X,\mathcal F)=0$ for every *coherent* $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$; (2) the same vanishing holds for every *quasi-coherent* $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$; (3) **no irreducible component of $X$ of maximal dimension $d$** (with its reduced induced scheme structure) is proper over $k$. It is allowed for proper irreducible components of *lower* dimension to exist. The nonempty and separated finite-type hypotheses must be retained.
standalone_statement_draft: Let $X$ be a **nonempty separated finite-type** scheme over a field $k$ with Krull dimension $d=\dim X$. The following conditions are equivalent: (1) $H^d(X,\mathcal F)=0$ for every *coherent* $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$; (2) the same vanishing holds for every *quasi-coherent* $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$; (3) **no irreducible component of $X$ of maximal dimension $d$** (with its reduced induced scheme structure) is proper over $k$. It is allowed for proper irreducible components of *lower* dimension to exist. The nonempty and separated finite-type hypotheses must be retained.
hypotheses: X nonempty separated finite type/k; d=dim X.
conclusions: Coherent top-degree vanishing, quasi-coherent top-degree vanishing and absence of proper maximal-dimensional components equivalent.
